v6 98.50 kept (seeds 0/11 98.50/97.68 vs v5 98.31/97.73): the B section gets a REAL RHODES SOLO instead of the theme generator. It is built in 4-bar phrases: a 3-note chord cell entered by a chromatic approach from below, the cell sequenced a step up, a sixteenth run up the Lydian mode, then a long landing note (the #4, the Lydian colour, on the last phrase). Each phrase starts a third higher, so the solo climbs and opens out over the harmonic wheel and hands the song to the trading horns.

v7 98.08 kept (seeds 0/11 98.08/97.76 vs v6 98.50/97.68, mean -0.17): the horns ANSWER the rhodes. The trades now open with the trumpet quoting the rhodes solo's last phrase (its chord cell with the chromatic approach) and the tenor answering with the cell a step up, both re-heard in F# Phrygian dominant, before they trade their own bars. The solo and the trades become one conversation instead of two sections.

v8 98.23 (seeds 0/11 98.23/97.66 vs v7 98.08/97.76): THE CELL COMES HOME at the climax. Over the stretched wheel (11/8, 13/8) the trumpet and tenor stop soloing and join the fretless on the NIGHT CELL in octaves (trumpet two octaves up, tenor one), breaking back out into their line every third bar. The climax is now the whole band hammering the song's first idea, which the intro set up on the bass alone.

v9 98.53 (seeds 0/11 98.53/98.52 vs v8 98.23/97.66): THE UNRAVELLING. The outro used to fade the whole band together; now the band leaves the vamp one voice every two bars - the wah, then the rhodes, then the trumpet's line and the doublings, then the kit - until the fretless and the sub play the NIGHT CELL alone under the fade, as the song began. The song closes the circle the intro opened, and the climax's full-band cell has somewhere to go.

v10 98.52 (seeds 0/11 98.52/98.52, level with v9): an ANSWER to chirper-two. Palindrome for Brushes and Toms plays this song's NIGHT CELL in its bridge; now Turnstile Hours' break answers with t4's own voice. Its tom choir (the singing physical toms, borrowed) sings t4's MIRROR MELODY over the bass and kit: the 3/4 cell (A G F E), the 5/8 cell (D E F), both retrograde the palindrome's way, then all of it a fourth up as the rhodes comes back. The break, which was bass and kit alone, now carries the album's conversation, about 9 dB under the mix.

v11 98.54 (seeds 0/11 98.54/98.54 vs v10 98.52/98.52): THE TRADES ARGUE. The trading bars used the theme generator, so trumpet and tenor took turns without listening. Now each trumpet bar develops one idea - a 4-note chord cell entered from a semitone below, sequenced a step higher each trade and broken into fragments (repeated pairs, rests between) as the section goes on - and each tenor bar answers the trumpet's last bar mirrored around its first note, an octave down. After the opening quote of the rhodes solo, the trades are now a conversation that builds into the climax.
